upper_paragraph_zone.description: Four lines of running Voynich text at the very top of the parchment, above all drawn illustrations. Lines f68r1.1–f68r1.4 form a standard paragraph block. Line f68r1.3 contains a single <-> bisection, suggesting a visual element (possibly the top arc of the sun face circle or a marginal line) intrudes into that text line.

sun_face_circle.description: A circular medallion drawn in the upper-center of the page below the paragraph text. Contains a stylized human face (eyes, nose, lips) with a decorative wreath-like or radiating border. Rendered in brown ink with tan/gold tones. The @Cc label (f68r1.37) is inscribed around or within this circle. This is the dominant illustration anchor of the folio.

moon_face_circle.description: A smaller circular medallion in the lower-center of the page, featuring a human face rendered with a blue painted crescent arc suggesting a crescent moon phase. Brown ink outlining. Positioned approximately two-thirds down the page. No dedicated @Cc label in this folio's transcription (the @Cc f68r1.37 belongs to the sun face), but the moon is visually labeled by nearby @Ls star-labels.

large_outer_arc.description: A large faint circular arc drawn in light ink, visible particularly in the right half of the folio, enclosing or framing a portion of the star field. Likely represents a celestial sphere or zodiac boundary.

star_field.description: Approximately 29 individual multi-pointed star drawings scattered across the page between the sun face circle and the moon face circle. Each star is rendered in tan/gold ink with 6–8 pointed rays. Each star has an immediately adjacent @Ls label (f68r1.8 through f68r1.36). Stars are distributed in a roughly organic arrangement without rigid rows.
